title: Cleaner return advances the blank prefix
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $\mathit{emit}\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and let $x,\mathit{arg},\mathit{cap}$ be Boolean words. For any time $T$ and source tape $i$, take the bank frame with the first $i$ data, interval-marker, origin-marker, and head entries blank, and the remaining entries taken from the run of $M$ on $\mathit{arg}$ at time $T$ (with the corresponding visited-span markers and head positions). Embedding the cleaner's three-tape configuration in cleaner state $3$, with its three tapes blank and heads at $0$, into the three slots for tape $i$ yields exactly the bank frame with the first $i+1$ entries blank and the cleaner in its return state for tape $i$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean input, argument, and capture words $x,\mathit{arg},\mathit{cap}$
replaced:
For every mode, input, argument and capture words, time $T$, and source tape $i$:
relocating the interval cleaner's blank return endpoint into the cleanup frame whose
first $i$ banks are blank yields the cleanup frame whose first $i + 1$ banks are blank,
in the cleaner-return control state for bank $i$.
